Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, lighting, and crop. Image2 provides only the mascot identity and anatomy. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body. The head must feature green-ringed black eyes and a mouth that matches the source expression. Preserve the actual bareheaded state with very short close-cut dark brown/black hair and a high receding hairline. Retain real dark brows and the small restrained dark/grey upper-lip moustache with a clean chin. Do not add spectacles, as none are visible in the source. Maintain the dark navy/charcoal open civilian suit with a white/pale shirt collar and a grey/blue necktie with limited pale diagonal pattern. Ensure the rounded chin immediately meets a raised and broadened existing neckline, creating a very short broad neck transition with minimal throat exposure. Avoid separate yellow neck shafts, pointed V funnels, pinched collars, neck rolls, floating collars, clipping, or cream belly bibs. Preserve the actual open garment state and coherent front/rear collar overlap with contact shadows. Retain the complete tilted dark frame, opaque photographic backing in its actual source color, and the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha transparency only outside the complete card silhouette. Do not invent insignia, text, or accessories. Keep fine primary details understated where they are indistinct in the source. Preserve the exact primary head angle, lighting, and crop from Image1.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: BAREHEADED nearly frontal/slightly angled bust, very short close-cut DARK BROWN/BLACK hair with high receding hairline, real brow HAIR, small restrained DARK/GREY upper-lip MOUSTACHE with clean chin, serious CLOSED mouth and no visible spectacles. Dark NAVY/CHARCOAL OPEN civilian suit with WHITE/PALE shirt collar and GREY/BLUE necktie with limited pale diagonal pattern visible beside note. Preserve suit lapels and actual neckwear, not a closed military tunic, bow tie or military regalia. Keep exact primary head angle, lighting and crop.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Do not copy human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit the original neckline around the compact rounded head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decorations hidden behind note. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
